title.narrative: Sustainable Fisheries Resources Development Project (Fourth South West Indian Ocean Fisheries Governance and Shared Growth Project)

description.narrative: The development objective of Sustainable Fisheries Resources Development Project for Maldives aims to improve management of fisheries at regional and national levels including support to establish mariculture in targeted atolls in the Maldives. This project has three components. 1) The first component, Augmentation of Institutional Capacity for Marine Fisheries Management, seeks to enhance the government's capacity to implement a more effective monitoring of the fisheries sector and internal control system of key marine fisheries value chains. It has the following four subcomponents: (i) development of key fisheries management and planning instruments; (ii) development and implementation of fisheries management activities; (iii) support to long-term program for fisheries management; and (iv) fisheries sector capacity building. 2) The second component Support to Mariculture and Diversification of Fisheries, has the following four subcomponents: (i) development and demonstration of mariculture production and technology package; (ii) promotion of mariculture out-grower schemes and seafood growth clusters; (iii) supporting design, construction and operation of a multispecies hatchery; and (iv) scoping of long-term marine fisheries diversification studies. 3) The third component, Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation, would provide equipment, technical assistance, training, and incremental operating cost to strengthen the overall administrative capacity and capability of the Ministry of Fisheries and Agriculture and its Project Management Unit (PMU).
To improve management of fisheries at regional and national levels including support to establish mariculture in targeted atolls inthe Maldives.

Viability demonstrated for out-grower farms of groupers (or other species equivalent in value)

comment.narrative:
<p>Substantially achieved the revised target (95 percent). The project supported initiation pilot grow-out of grouper mariculture in 2019, after the 2017-18 period was used to train interested household level entrepreneurs, and to secure procurement of mariculture cages, fingerlings and fish feed. The initial batch of production was ready for sale by May-June 2020, but could be sold onlyin August 2020 due to the COVID-19 disruptions. The second batch of production was also completed for 5 of the 19 pilot farms. Remaining pilot farms are continuing restocking with the supply of fingerlings from the research-scale hatchery established and operating at Maniyafushi. Viability of the grow-out farms was demonstrated by auction of produce, where the sale prices received generated substantial profit to the household level enterprises. Of the 20 targeted pilot farms, one farm could not be supported due to ownership issues discovered by the Island Council, who advised against continuing supporting this particular farm. </p>
<p>Partly achieved the original target (9.5 percent). The original target of establishing 200 grow-out farms was not achieved due to the impacts of the the COVID-19 pandemic. In addition to the pilot farms, 135 additional grow-out farms are ready to be rolled out subject to ensuring the supply of fingerlings. As per the MoFMRA plans and budgets, the construction of the multispecies hatchery at Maanaagalaa Island will be completed in November 2023, supply of fingerlings will start from March 2024, and the original target of establishing production and sale from 200 grow-out farms will be achieved by December 2024. Additionally, the MoFMRA plans to roll-out another 400 grow-out farms by incentivizing small and medium private sector enterprises in the next 3 years. </p>

title.narrative: Vessels complying with IOTC requirements on monitoring and reporting
Vessels complying with IOTC requirements on monitoring and reporting

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved the revised target (100 percent). To enable inspection under the MCS regime, state-of-art vessel locating devices capable of two-way communication and real-time data transfer to the MoFMRA fisheries information system was installed and commissioned in all marine (tuna) fishing vessels in Maldives. The IOTC resolutions require all tuna fishing vessels above 24 meter length to be inspected under MCS. In Maldives, all vessels above 18 meter length are covered now. This is now part of the licensing requirement, renewed annually. Note that 37 of these 680 vessels have not resumed fishing since the COVID-19 outbreak. [Note that even if the achievement was 680 in comparison to the target of 670, this should be taken only as 100 percent achievement rather than exceeding the target, as the intent was to cover all tuna fishing vessels above 18 meter in length, which is the case here).</p>

<p>Achieved the original target (100 percent). The original target of 1,100 vessels were the estimated number of tuna fishing vessels in 2016 (when there was no licensing regime). Over a period of time, owners of multiple small vessels replaced those with larger vessels. The estimate came down to 732 in 2018 after a survey. By end of 2021, when all vessel owners were contacted, the estimate was 670. Note that this reduction of target did not reduce the scope of the project. The original intent was to cover all marine (tuna) fishing vessels. The same intent was there at the restructuring. No marine (tuna) fishing vessel is excluded. </p>

<p>The MoFMRA has also started installing and commissioning appropriate and relatively low-cost vessel locating devices on about 200 smaller vessels engagd in fishing. These vessels are not counted as achievement as the original intent did not cover the reef fishing vessels, and where no IOTC or other international inspection compliance requirements apply.  </p>

title.narrative: Operational capacity for production and supply of fingerlings in place

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved the revised indicator (100 percent). The operational capacity for production and supply of fingerlings is established as: (i) the quarantine facility is now fully capable of processing imports of at least 20,000 fingerlings per month, as has beendemonstrated during the 3 batches of imports, for a total of 57,000 grouper fingerlings where quarantine was completed successfully; (ii) construction of a hatchery with all necessary installations including biosecurity measures had been completed at Maniyafushi island with a capacity of producing a total of at least 150,000 fingerlings per month, and, (iii) 30 requisite operational staff with needed qualification have been trained in the process of hatchery operations, that has created a skill base for the larger operation of the multispecies hatchery under construction and likely to be operational by December 2023. Overall, the project has already produced or imported about 200,000 fingerlings to supply to grow-out farms.</p>
<p>Partly achieved the original indicator (7 percent). This revised indicator replaced the original indicator of "Production of fingerlings by the hatchery" (target number 2,000,000). The production of fingerling in the country has been about 140,000. The shortfall is mainly caused by the delay in establishing the multispecies hatchery, owing mainly to the COVID-19 pandemic, but which is now under construction through a private sector concession, and is expected to be operational by November 2023, and therefore, fingerling supplies would resume in March 2024 and the original target is likely to be achieved during 2024-25, with a delay of about 18-21 months. Meanwhile, the current small facility at Maniyafushi will continue production. </p>

<p>Achieved the revised target introduced at restructuring (100 percent). As per agreed during restructuring, the following were completed: (i) all processes for commercial supply of inputs required for mariculture (cages, fingerlings, and fish feed) are established; (ii) a small-scale hatchery is established, operational, producing and supplying grouper  fingerlings to pilot out-grower farms, while the construction of a larger multispecies hatchery is underway through a concession to a private joint venture firm; (iii) a quarantine facility is established and fully operational to facilitate supplementary import of fingerlings; (iv) another 135 mariculture cage farms are ready to start production once supply of fingerling resumes when the multispecies hatchery is operational; and (v) 19 compared to the target 20 out-grower farms have completed one batch of production and sold the harvested fish products at a profit, 5 of these farms did it twice  - showing mariculture is now established and operational in Maldives.</p>
<p>Partly achieved the original target (4.1 percent). At restructuring this indicator replaced the original indicator "Value of production from mariculture supported by the project" (target - US$9 million). Only a small part of the target for the original indicator was achieved (the total value of production so far is US$365,000). At restructuring, it was evident thatdue to impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic (delay in establishing the multispecies hatchery, stoppage of import of fingerlings and fish feed during most of 2020-21, and unviability of increased price of imported fingerlings since then) this target would not be reached within the project closing date. However, the multispecies hatchery (under construction through a concession to a private sector joint venture) is expected to be operational by December 2023, and the that original target is likely to be achieved by December 2024.</p>

title.narrative: Operational capacity for production and supply of fingerlings in place

comment.narrative: Although (i) the quarantine facility is capable of processing imports of at least 20,000 fingerlings per month; and, (ii) 24 of the 30 requisite operational staff with needed qualification and training are in place to operate the hatcheries, the construction of hatcheries with a capacity of producing a total of at least 150,000 fingerlings per month is yet to be completed.

Cumulative targets. Price data will be the based on the regular market surveys (Hong Kong and Singapore).
Hugely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic, as even the grow-out farms who completed the first batch of production could not be supplied with fingerlings and fish feed as imports were stopped since August 2020. The project (Component B) is obviously significantly behind. As per the workplans prepared by MoFMRA at the MTR, significant improvement was expected between July 2021 and June 2022, part of which did not take place as import of fingerlings could not resume. However, with production of fingerlings restarting at the hatchery at Maniyafushi Research-scale hatchery, the target is on track to be achieved prior to the closing date. MoFMRA is taking steps t maximize the stocking so that the target is achieved (even after the project closing date, in which case the residual expenditure will be financed by the MoFMRA).

comment.narrative:
Annual targets. Supporting the capacity will include convening, organizing and facilitating joint negotiation stance (described in a joint draft) prior to each IOTC annual meeting.
MoFA has organized and supported the G16 Coastal States Meeting on Allocation Principles at Seychelles in February 2018 prior to the IOTC Annual Session in May 2018. A second meeting of the G16 Coastal States was organized at Cape Town, South Africa on October 13-14, 2018 (following the SWIOFC meeting at Cape Town, to optimize expenses), and a third meeting at Male, Maldives on January 13-14, 2019. Maldives is actively working with like minded countries to schedule a similar support ahead of the upcoming IOTC annual meeting. The planned events of March 2020 could not yet take place due to COVID-19 pandemic. However, in early 2021, Maldives organized several rounds of meetings with G16 Coastal States for reparation for the IOTC meetings (organized virtually) in April 2021. In the IOTC meeting Maldives sponsored proposals for better management and limiting quota for yellowfin tuna. Later, during the IOTC plenary, Maldives and EU moved joint proposals that were taken up for consideration. Since he IOTC Plenary, Maldives have pursued active dialogues with several members states of IOTC in support of thei proposal. In 2022, Maldives hosted the G-16 countries to pursue joint negotiation stances.

Pursuant to the 2019 Fisheries Act, eight Regulations were drafted, consulted with a wide spectrum of stakeholders, finalzed, adopted, and notified during August-October 2020. Additionally, six other regulations were drafted and stakeholder consultations were undertaken in 2021-2022. These are not counted as finalization and notification is yet to take place. </p>

On-Board Vessel Electronic Observation System established and operational

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved revised target (100 percent). As per the IOTC recommendations, 5 percent of the fishing trips are to be monitored. To comply with this requirement, 15 electronic observer systems were installed, tested, used, and software integration achieved with theMoFMRA fisheries information system, and used to observe the type of catch and fishing efforts. This is also integrated with the locational information available real-time from the vessel locating devices installed in the marine (tuna) fishing fleet. </p>
<p>Partly achieved the original target (39.8 percent). The revised indicator was introduced at the restructuring in May 2022 replacing the original indicator "Fishing trips covered with Electronic observation" (target - 6,000 trips). Against this original target only 2,385 trips were covered with electronic observation. Although the electronic observer systems were installed in February-March 2020, the testing and commissioning of the equipment could only be completed in late 2021 due to COVID-19 pandemic. Software integration and optimization took additional time. However, all electronic observer systems were fully operational and the target of 5 percent of fishing trips to be covered under electronic observation will be achieved in 2024. Therefore, the revised target did not indicate any reduction of scope of the project activity. </p>

title.narrative: On-Board Vessel Electronic Observation System established and operational

comment.narrative:
Annual targets. As per IOTC recommendations 5% of all fishing trips (total trips are 100,000 per year). Therefore, for 100% compliance, the number of trips required is 5,000, while the Project target is 6,000.
Achievements of the targets were linked to procurement of the contract for the electronic observer systems. The actual observation, after pre-trial period after installation,nbsp;started by March 2020, but was disrupted by lockdown and lack of export since early March 2020 due to COVID-19 pandemic. Reduced fishing trips meant that by December 2020 (Year 3), the trips were below 1,000. Continued impacts of COVID-19 pandemic now means that the final target will be completed only by October-November 2022, one or two months ahead of the current project closing date (compared to the original estimate of completing this activity at least 9 to 12 months ahead of the project closing date). To meet the target in the current situation of uncertainty due to pandemic, the project has procured an additional 5-10 numbers of such devices. However, the On-Board Vessel Electronic Observation System established and is operational.

Mariculture Research and Development Facility is completed and operational

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved this revised target (100 percent). The Mariculture Research and Development facility is completed and operational as: (i) all requisite infrastructure and equipment for carrying the intended research and training of the target groups are in place; (ii) the research program was successful in establishment of culture practices of at least two native or endemic fish species; (iii) the commercial hatching and production processes for at least two fish species was demonstrated; and (iv) the requisite number ofqualified and experienced staff are in place to operate the science program, to operate the facility and to conduct training program for the target groups for future mariculture development in Maldives.</p>
<p>Partially achieved target for the original indicator: "Viability demonstrated for out-grower farms of sea cucumber (or other species equivalent in value)" (target - increase in number of such farms by 150 over the baseline of 100). The baseline of 100 sea cucumber farms were financed by another donor-financed project in Maldives (Mariculture Enterprise Development Project) increased to 115, but all these farms stopped during the COVID-19 period. As a result the planned expansion could not take off. However, going forward the fingerlings would be produced by the multispecies hatchery under construction, and the MoFMRA will encourage private sector to take up farming of sea cucumbers using clear commercial practices. The MMRDF is working on improving culture techniques of two varieties of sea cucumber so that the technical concerns about using imported sea cucumber fingerlings can be resolved. The dropping of this indicator at restructuring indicates a reduction of scope of Component B, or at least an acknowledgement that the originally intended development of sea cucumber mariculture will be delayed by at least two years. </p>
